Imagine a Mosasaurus suddenly appeared in the ocean today.
What would happen to you?
You are on a beach on a hot summer day.
Kids.
Surfboards.
Seagulls.
You swim out past the waves.
The water is calm and blue.
Then a shadow passes beneath you.
Longer than a bus.
Then.
The surface explodes.
A Mosasaurus could grow up to fifteen metres long.
Its jaws had a hinge in the middle, and a second row of teeth on the roof of its mouth.
It did not chew.
It swallowed prey whole.
It was not a fish, and not a dinosaur.
It was a giant sea lizard that breathed air.
Sharks, dolphins, even whales.
Nothing in today's ocean would be safe.
But…
The very first Mosasaurus was found near Maastricht, in the Netherlands.
Its name means "lizard of the Meuse".
In 1795, French soldiers took the skull as war loot.
It is still in Paris today.
So remember.
The ocean was once ruled by a lizard longer than a bus.
Would you still go swimming?
